To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
relatives of early-onset cases have an increased breast cancer risk, and that the risk is increased for relatives of cases without a BRAC1 or BRAC2 mutation.

the incidence of breast cancer in relatives of women with early onset breast cancer is increased irrespective of the BRACA mutation status in the family and that the risk of breast and prostate cancer increases with decreasing age of onset and with increasing number affected relatives.

the breast cancer risk is increased in first-degree relatives of women with early onset breast cancer, irrespective of their BRCA mutation status, and that this risk increases with decreasing age of onset and with increasing number affected relatives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the incidence of cancer in relatives of early-onset cases of breast cancer.
the identification of genes and genetic pathways that predispose to early-onset breast and other cancers.
the identification and characterization of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the cell fate of stem cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
early-onset breast cancers are associated with a high familial risk, but the underlying cause of this risk is unknown.
the risk for breast cancer is increased in relatives of early-onset cases, but the risk is lower than that of relatives of late-onset breast cancer.
the risk of cancer in FDRs is increased in early-onset breast cancers and that the risk is increased for all cancers except ovarian cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incidence of cancer in relatives of early-onset cases with breast cancer is increased irrespective of the presence of a BRCA mutation.
the incidence of breast cancer increases with decreasing age at onset of the disease in relatives of early-onset cases.
the risk for breast cancer is increased in relatives of early-onset cases, irrespective of their mutation status.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of cancer is increased for relatives of women with early onset breast cancer.
the risk of breast and other cancers is increased for relatives of women with early onset breast cancer, irrespective of the presence or absence of a BRCA mutation in their family.
we found an increased risk of breast cancer for first-degree relatives of women diagnosed with early-onset (before the age of 41 years) breast cancer.
